newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's appoints new anti-Mafia chief.
newsitem.headline: Italy's appoints new anti-Mafia chief.

text.p: Florence prosecutor Pier Luigi Vigna, head of a high-profile probe into a series of Mafia bombings in Italy three years ago, was named on Friday as the country's top anti-Mafia investigator.
The Superior Council of Magistrates, the ruling body of the Italian judiciary, said it had elected Vigna to succeed Bruno Siclari as head of the National Anti-Mafia Directorate.
Siclari's term had expired and his request to stay on for another year was turned down.

The Italian media had reported that Vigna's main rival for the job was Francesco Saverio Borrelli, the chief Milan prosecutor who has led the broad "Tangentopoli" (Bribesville) corruption probes over the past few years.

Vigna, Florence's chief prosecuting magistrate, said he was "naturally satisfied" about his new job, which involves leading and coordinating Italy's top Mafia probes. He said one of his main tasks would be to crack down on Mafia money laundering.
"If we can take the money away from the Mafia, then we not only weaken the criminal organisation but clean up the economy as well," he told reporters.
Vigna has a long record of investigating the Mafia, becoming a household name for his probe into the bombings that hit Rome, Florence and Milan in the summer of 1993, killing 10 people.

Around 35 alleged mobsters, including "Godfather" Salvatore Riina, have been accused in connection with the attacks. Their trial is due to open next Tuesday in Florence, where the world-famous Uffizi Gallery was among the bomb targets.
Vigna has said he believed the Mafia carried out two bomb attacks against churches in Rome in the campaign to punish Pope John Paul for speaking out against the Mafia in Sicily in 1993.
